questions.stem: The line through $A=(k,2k+1)$ and $B=(3,5)$ is perpendicular to $y=2x+7$. Find the exact area of the triangle whose vertices are O=(0,0), A and B.

options.errorPath: Omit the triangle factor 1/2.
Report k instead of the area.
Report the y-coordinate of A.
Report the vertical separation of A and B.
Report the horizontal separation of A and B.

workedSolutionSteps: The line AB has gradient −1/2 and passes through B, so y=−x/2+13/2. Equating this with 2k+1 gives k=11/5 and A=(11/5,27/5).
At x=11/5 the line OB, whose equation is y=5x/3, has height 11/3. The vertical separation from A is 27/5−11/3=26/15.
Split triangle OAB at this vertical segment: its two triangle areas add to half the segment length times the total horizontal width 3. Thus area=(26/15)×3/2=13/5.

questions.stem: For integer k with $2\le k\le15$, the line through $(1,2)$ and $(k,k+4)$ has gradient m. Find the sum of all k for which $1<m\le\frac74$ and the y-intercept is at most $\frac23$.

options.errorPath: Use the gradient restriction only, summing k=5,…,15.
Report the number of feasible values.
Omit k=10, treating the y-intercept bound as strict.
Report only the largest feasible k.
Include k=5 twice when summing the permitted integers.

workedSolutionSteps: m=1+3/(k−1), with k>1. The bound m≤7/4 requires k−1≥4, hence k≥5.
The intercept is c=2−m=1−3/(k−1). Requiring c≤2/3 gives 3/(k−1)≥1/3, hence k≤10.
Thus k=5,…,10 inclusive. The sum is 6(5+10)/2=45.

Area=27 implies (9/2)×OQ/2=27, hence Q=(12,0).

Comparing with C: 12+3n<24+2n gives n<12. The budget gives n≤12.
Thus n=9,10,11 and the sum is 30.

A(t)≥1.5t gives t≤40. B(t)−A(t)=t/4−5≥3 gives t≥32.
The real interval is [32,40], length 8.

workedSolutionSteps: P=(2,5); the smaller triangle is similar to the original, with width ratio (2−k)/2.
If its area is one ninth of the remainder, its fraction of the original area is 1/10. Hence ((2−k)/2)²=1/10.

Require y to have the same parity as x. For x=0,1,2,3,4 the counts are 7,5,4,2,1 respectively.
The counts sum to 7+5+4+2+1=19.

questions.stem: A point P lies on $y=x+1$ and is equally distant from A(0,0) and B(6,2). A second point Q lies on the same line and $OQ^2=OP^2$, where O is the origin. Find the x-coordinate of Q, given Q≠P.

Reflect P's x-coordinate in zero instead of using the symmetry of the quadratic.

Report the midpoint of the two x-coordinates.

For any point on the line, squared distance to O is 2x²+2x+1=2(x+1/2)²+1/2.
The equal-distance inputs are symmetric about x=−1/2, so their sum is −1. The other x is −1−9/4=−13/4.

questions.stem: A circle has centre (2,3) and passes through O=(0,0). A horizontal line $y=k$ intersects the circle at two distinct points A and B with integer x-coordinates and integer k. Find the sum of all possible positive integer k.

options.errorPath: Report only the greatest eligible positive k.
Report the number of eligible positive k.
Include k=3 even though the intersections are not integral.
Omit the eligible value k=1.
Omit the eligible value k=5.

workedSolutionSteps: The radius squared is 13, so (x−2)²=13−(k−3)².
For two distinct integral x-values, the right side must be a positive perfect square. The only integer-square decompositions of 13 are 4+9 and 9+4.
Thus k=3±2 or 3±3, giving 0,1,5,6. The positive values 1,5,6 sum to 12.

questions.stem: A line through (2,3) crosses both positive axes. The area of its axis-intercept triangle is 18. Find the sum of the two possible y-intercepts.

options.errorPath: Report the midpoint of the two possible y-intercepts.
Report their product rather than their sum.
Report the product of the x- and y-intercepts for either line.
Report the sum of the two x-intercepts instead of the y-intercepts.
Use the point's y-coordinate twice instead of solving for intercepts.

workedSolutionSteps: Let positive intercepts be a on x-axis and b on y-axis. Area gives ab=36. Since (2,3) lies on the line, 2/a+3/b=1.
Multiply by ab: 2b+3a=36. Substitute a=36/b to get 2b²−36b+108=0, or b²−18b+54=0.
Both roots 9±3√3 are positive and give a=36/b>0. Their sum is 18.

questions.stem: Three instruments give readings A=2x+3, B=5x−9 and C=4x−5 for nonnegative integer x. Find the sum of all inputs for which the largest reading minus the smallest is at most 6 and A is not the largest reading (a tie for largest is excluded).

options.errorPath: Report the number of eligible inputs.
Report the smallest eligible input.
Sum every input from 2 to 6, without requiring A not to be largest.
Report the largest valid input.
Include x=4 despite the three-way tie.

workedSolutionSteps: The range is at most 6 exactly when all three pairwise differences are at most 6. From |A−B|=|12−3x|≤6 get 2≤x≤6.
|A−C|=|8−2x|≤6 gives 1≤x≤7; |B−C|=|x−4|≤6 gives −2≤x≤10, so no further restriction.
For x≤4, A is largest or tied; for x>4 it is strictly below both B and C. Thus x=5,6 sum to 11.

Triangle base on y-axis is 16/3 and height 8/3; area=64/9.

workedSolutionSteps: The segment equation is y=6−3x/4. At P, x=2y, giving x=24/5. At Q, y=2x, giving x=24/11.
The horizontal distance between P and Q is 24/5−24/11=144/55. Both points are on the same segment, so length ratios equal horizontal distance ratios.
Divide by the full horizontal length 8: PQ:AB=18:55.
